en: The Legend of the Elder Uruvelakassapa From the Kaccāyana Chapter of the Therāpadāna, Number Eight I was a young brahmin, well-versed in the Vedas, A student of the three Vedas, possessing great wisdom. At that time, the Teacher of the World, the Buddha, Was dwelling in the city of Rājagaha. Having heard of his fame, I went to see him; There I saw the Great Sage, seated upon a stone slab. With a heart full of faith, I paid homage to him, And sat down to one side, listening to the Dhamma. Then the Teacher, knowing my disposition, Expounded the Dhamma that leads to liberation. Hearing the Dhamma, my mind became clear and pure; I took refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha. I offered alms-food to the Teacher, And requested ordination from the World-Honored One. The Teacher, out of compassion for me, Granted me the going-forth and the higher ordination. Having become a monk, I applied myself with diligence; In no long time, I attained the goal of the holy life. I realized for myself, through direct knowledge, That birth had been exhausted and the holy life fulfilled. I am a Worthy One (Arhat), cool and peaceful; My burden is laid down, and I have lived the life. By this meritorious deed, throughout many births, I was never born in a state of misery. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I dwelt in the heavens, enjoying celestial bliss. When my lifespan there came to an end, I was reborn in the human world. In every birth, I was handsome and fair-skinned, Possessing great strength and noble lineage. Through the power of that wholesome deed, I have now attained the fruit of Arhatship. I have seen the Buddha, the Teacher of the World, And I have heard the Dhamma that is so hard to find. Having fulfilled all the perfections, I have reached the end of suffering. This is the legend of the Elder Uruvelakassapa, The eighth in the Kaccāyana Chapter.
“The Victor named Padumuttara,
the Sage who knows all the world,
[lived] one hundred thousand aeons ago from now.”
In that eon, the Visionary One appeared.
He was the instructor, the enlightener,
and the deliverer of all living beings.
The Buddha, skilled in teaching,
has delivered many people;
he is compassionate and merciful.
Seeking the welfare of all living beings,
he established all the heretics who arrived there in the five precepts.
Thus it was free from confusion and empty of non-Buddhist sectarians,
yet variegated with Arahants.
By those who have attained mastery and reached the state of the "Tādi," that Great Sage has risen up, possessing eighty-four thousand qualities of the Jewels.
Resembling a priceless golden ornament,
endowed with the thirty-two excellent marks,
for one hundred thousand years—
As long as life remains,
for that long he remained,
and thereby delivered many people.
At that time, a brahmin highly esteemed as virtuous in Haṃsavatī,
having approached the Lamp of the World, said:
I heard the teaching of the Dhamma.
At that time, in the great assembly,
among the great assembly of disciples;
Having heard that he was being established as the foremost among these,
I was filled with joy along with a great retinue.
Having invited the Great Conqueror together with a thousand brahmins,
I gave the gift along with them.
Having given a great gift and paid homage to the Leader,
he stood to one side, joyful.
I spoke these words:
“O Hero, because of my faith in you and because of the quality of my service;”
"Let there be a great assembly wherever I am reborn.
Then he spoke to the assembly:
With a voice like the trumpeting of an elephant and the cry of the karavīka bird, the Teacher said:
"Behold this brahmin!"
The golden-hued one with mighty arms,
whose face and eyes are like lotuses,
joyful and with uplifted limbs.
"He possesses faith in my virtues.
This man aspires to the status of the monk Sīhaghosa."
In a future time,
you shall obtain that heart's desire.
In a hundred thousand aeons,
Born of the Okkāka clan,
he will be a teacher in the world named Gotama by lineage.
His heir in the Dhammas,
his own legitimate son, fashioned by the Dhamma,
Kassapa by clan.
‘He shall become a disciple of the Teacher.
Ninety-two aeons from now,
there was a peerless Teacher;
Peerless and incomparable,
Phussa, the leader supreme in the world—
having destroyed all darkness, he...
Having disentangled the great tangle,
he rains down the rain of the Deathless,
satisfying the world together with its devas.
For at that time, in Bārāṇasī,
we were the king and his two brothers;
all three of us were brothers.
They were indeed well-integrated with the king—
heroic in form, powerful,
and unconquered in battle.
Then the lord of the earth said to us:
"Go now and proceed to the border region."
"Having cleared the power of the forest wilderness,
and having made it secure and free from disease,
give it back again"— thus you should speak.
Then we said to him:
"If you would give us the Leader,
for our service."
We shall accomplish it for you from there.
Then, having obtained the boon,
we were dispatched by the protector of the earth.
Having laid down the sword at the borderlands and returned once more,
he requested permission to attend upon the Teacher.
Having obtained the King, the Leader of the World,
the Hero among Sages,
we made offerings to him for as long as we lived.
Expensive garments and exquisite flavors,
and delightful dwellings—
Having given beneficial medicines to the Sage together with the Saṅgha— medicines produced by us in accordance with the Dhamma—
Virtuous, compassionate,
with minds intent on meditation,
those endowed with faith, having rendered service,
With a mind of loving-kindness toward the Leader; when he,
the supreme one in the world, has attained nibbāna,
having performed worship according to one's ability.
Passing away from there, we all went to the Santuṣita heaven,
where we experienced great bliss.

This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a magician displays many various forms in the theater, so too does the Blessed One manifest diverse manifestations for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a skilled painter, with pigments and a brush, paints various beautiful forms upon a wall, so too does the Blessed One manifest diverse manifestations for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a skilled goldsmith fashions various ornaments from a single nugget of gold, so too does the Blessed One manifest diverse manifestations for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single lamp, when placed in a house, dispels all darkness, so too does the Blessed One, though one, dispel the darkness of ignorance for the world of gods and humans. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single moon, reflected in many vessels of water, appears as many moons, so too does the Blessed One, though one, appear as many for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single sound, when uttered by a drum, produces many different sounds according to the beating of the drum, so too does the Blessed One, though one, produce diverse teachings for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single cloud rains down water everywhere upon the earth, so too does the Blessed One, though one, rain down the rain of Dhamma for the sake of training beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single sun, rising in the sky, illuminates the entire world with its rays, so too does the Blessed One, though one, illuminate the world with the light of wisdom. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single great ocean contains immeasurable waters, so too does the Blessed One, though one, possess immeasurable qualities. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single mountain, such as Sineru, is immovable and firm, so too is the Blessed One unshakable by any worldly phenomena. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single diamond pierces through all other gems, so too does the Blessed One, with the diamond of his wisdom, pierce through the thickets of all views. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single king, ruling over the four continents, brings peace and security to the world, so too does the Blessed One, the King of Dhamma, bring peace and security to the world of gods and humans. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single physician, possessing the knowledge of medicine, heals the diseases of many people, so too does the Blessed One, the Great Physician, heal the disease of suffering for the world of gods and humans. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single boat carries many people across the great river, so too does the Blessed One carry many beings across the ocean of saṃsāra. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single lamp, though small, dispels great darkness, so too does the Blessed One, though one, dispel the great darkness of ignorance. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single seed, when planted in the earth, grows into a vast forest, so too does the Blessed One, from a single root of merit, bring forth immeasurable fruits of liberation. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single cloud, though one, nourishes the crops of the whole world, so too does the Blessed One, with a single teaching, bring maturity to the faculties of many beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single fire, when kindled, consumes a great heap of fuel, so too does the Blessed One, with the fire of his wisdom, consume the fuel of defilements. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single mirror reflects all forms without exception, so too does the Blessed One, with the mirror of his omniscience, reflect the nature of all phenomena. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single drum, when struck, resounds throughout the city, so too does the Blessed One, with the drum of Dhamma, awaken the sleepers in the world. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single sun, rising at dawn, causes the lotuses to bloom, so too does the Blessed One cause the lotuses of the hearts of beings to bloom with the light of Dhamma. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single raincloud pours down rain everywhere upon the earth, so too does the Blessed One pour down the rain of Dhamma upon the field of beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single jewel, when held in the hand, fulfills all desires, so too does the Blessed One fulfill the wishes of all beings who take refuge in him. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single king, possessing the seven treasures, rules over the earth, so too does the Blessed One, possessing the seven treasures of the noble ones, rule over the world of gods and humans. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single lion, dwelling in the forest, roars fearlessly, so too does the Blessed One, the Lion of Men, roar the lion’s roar in the assemblies. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single moon, moving through the sky, is seen by all beings, so too is the Blessed One seen by all beings, bringing joy to their hearts. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single wind blows everywhere upon the world, so too does the Blessed One, with the wind of his compassion, blow upon all beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single tree, laden with fruit, provides sustenance for many birds, so too does the Blessed One provide the fruit of liberation for many beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single lamp, though small, dispels great darkness, so too does the Blessed One dispel the darkness of ignorance with the light of his wisdom. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single river flows toward the great ocean, so too do all wholesome roots flow toward the Blessed One. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single mountain peak is high and firm, so too is the Blessed One supreme and steadfast among all beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Blessed One. Just as a single sun, shining in the sky, illuminates the entire world, so too does the Blessed One illuminate the world with the light of his omniscience. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Just as a single cloud, though one, brings rain to all lands, so too does the Blessed One, with a single teaching, bring benefit to all beings. This is the fruit of making offerings to the Buddha. Thus wandering through existence,
I was once the lord of Videha,
by virtue of the words of Guṇāceḷa.
Possessing an inclination toward wrong view,
he has entered the path to hell because of my daughter Rucā.
Having failed to accept the advice given by Brahmā Nārada,
though I was exhorted by him in many ways, I remained.
Having abandoned evil views,
and having fulfilled the ten courses of wholesome action here with distinction;
Having cast off the body,
I went to heaven as if to my own abode.
When my final existence was reached,
I was a nominal Brahmin;
born in the great family of a brahmin in the prosperous city of Bārāṇasī.
Fearing death, disease, and old age,
having plunged into the great forest,
seeking the state of nibbāna—
I went forth among the Jaṭilas.
At that time, two brothers of mine also went forth together with me.
Having built a hermitage at Uruvelā, I dwelt there;
I was known by the clan name Kassapa.
I was a resident of Uruvelā;
from that time on, my designation became "Uruvelakassapa."
Near the river lived my brother,
known by the name of Nadī-Kassapa;
he was called by his own name.
This Gayā Kassapa was from Gayā.
His younger brother had two hundred followers,
and his middle brother had three hundred.
I had no fewer than five hundred disciples,
all of whom followed me.
Then the Buddha approached me.
Having performed various miracles,
the Leader of the World,
the Charioteer of Men, disciplined [beings].
With a retinue of a thousand,
I was one for whom the "Come, monk" formula was used;
together with all of them, I—
I attained arahantship.
Those very disciples and many others surrounded me.
And since I am capable of teaching,
therefore, O Seventh Sage,
amidst this great assembly, [I have spoken].
He placed me in this foremost position:
"Aha! The service rendered to the Buddha has borne fruit for me."
The defilements have been burnt away by me; ... [as before] ...
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Uruvelakassapa speak these verses.
This is the eighth *apadāna* of the elder Uruvelakassapa.
